name: Boiler circulation pumps / forced-circulation pumps (HRSG, once-through, controlled circulation)
description: In forced/controlled-circulation HRSGs and boilers, a pump circulates water/steam-water mixture from the drum through parallel evaporator circuits and back, maintaining tube-wall wetting where natural density head is insufficient (horizontal tubes, limited drum-to-evaporator height, long circuits). Natural-circulation and once-through units need no circulation pump in normal operation (once-through with superimposed circulation uses one at start-up/low load). Primary source: https://www.esteemprojects.com/library/HRSG-Design/page7_1.html

name: Stack/breeching dampers, bypass dampers and sealing systems for HRSG simple-cycle operation
description: Diverter/bypass damper systems route gas-turbine exhaust either to the bypass stack (simple cycle, HRSG offline) or through the HRSG (combined cycle), with mechanically interlocked isolation and seal-air systems so personnel can enter the isolated HRSG while the turbine runs. Stack dampers slow HRSG cooling between starts, prevent rain ingress and provide overpressure relief. Primary source: https://www.forneycorp.com/articles/hrsg-bypass-dampers

name: Induced-draft fan, stack and FGR ducting
description: Induced-draft fan and flue-gas path that maintain furnace draft and discharge products to stack. Stacks and ductwork are engineered from flue-gas volume, temperature and space constraints; dampers hold a set draft loss and an SCR reactor house is sized from the catalyst mass required to meet the emission limit. name: Boiler soot blower and online cleaning
description: Online cleaning equipment that removes ash and soot deposits from heat-transfer surfaces to preserve efficiency, keep flue-gas temperatures within design and prevent gas-passage blockage. Saturated steam is the most widely used blowing medium because boiler-generated steam is available; SCR catalyst cleaning uses much lower steam velocity to avoid mechanical or erosive damage. name: Boiler steam drum and mud drum
description: In drum-type water-tube boilers the upper steam drum is the point of steam/water separation and feedwater introduction, while the lower mud drum collects sediment; downcomers carry cooler dense water to the lower drum and risers return the heated mixture. Drum temperature stratification during cycling drives humping and connection stress, so drum design and circulation are central to load-change capability. Primary source: https://spiraxsarco.com/learn-about-steam/the-boiler-house/water-tube-boilers?sc_lang=en-GB

specifications.basis: Spirax Sarco: water-tube boilers with steam drums handle steam up to 160 bar
